findings.title: Delete condition for retryCount is global, not scoped to SMS method
findings.body: The OR clause `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of method (EMAIL, SMS, WHATSAPP). Since retryCount is only incremented in this SMS-specific handler, this may be fine today, but it is a latent bug: if retryCount is ever reused by other reminder types, this unscoped condition will delete unrelated reminders. It should be scoped with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` as well to avoid unintended data loss.

findings.title: Reminders with empty/missing message or sendTo are retried indefinitely
findings.body: When `message` is falsy or `sendTo` is missing, the code silently skips both the success and retry-increment branches (lines 158-188). Such reminders remain `scheduled: false` forever and are picked up again every cron run without ever incrementing retryCount or being cleaned up, unlike failures caught by try/catch or the twilio.scheduleSMS failure path. This creates reminders that loop indefinitely rather than being retried-and-deleted per the stated intent of the PR.

findings.title: No test coverage added for new retry/delete logic
findings.body: This PR changes core scheduling/deletion behavior (adding retryCount increments and deletion when retryCount > 1) but includes no new or updated tests verifying that reminders are retried, incremented, and eventually deleted as expected. This is a behavioral change with data-deletion consequences and should have test coverage.
